biography: Justin Armstrong's racing journey began not on a track, but on the winding country lanes of his childhood home in rural Oxfordshire. The son of a mechanic, he spent countless hours tinkering with engines, developing an innate understanding of machinery. His racing career was sparked by a chance encounter at a local hill climb event, where he impressed onlookers with his raw talent behind the wheel of a borrowed Caterham. This led to a foray in single-seater racing, experiencing moderate success, before finding his niche in GT racing. While he showed early promise, his inherent inconsistency has plagued his entire career. A defining moment came at the Spa 24 Hours in 2018 when, leading in the final hour, he crashed out due to a lapse in concentration. Now, at 34, Armstrong finds himself struggling to secure competitive drives, his star having seemingly faded.
drivingStyle: Armstrong's driving style is characterized by flashes of brilliance intertwined with moments of inexplicable error. When on form, he exhibits remarkable car control and daring overtaking maneuvers, particularly in wet conditions. However, he tends to overdrive the car, pushing it beyond its limits, which often leads to costly mistakes. Tire management is not his strength, and he struggles to maintain consistent pace throughout long stints. Under pressure, Armstrong's inconsistency is amplified, making him prone to unforced errors.

rivalries.reason: A bitter feud began after Rossi accused Armstrong of deliberately blocking him during qualifying at Silverstone, costing Rossi a front-row start.
They clashed multiple times on track in the Caterham Superlight series, resulting in several on-track incidents and post-race arguments.
Armstrong and Tanaka were teammates for a season but Tanaka felt Armstrong was getting preferential treatment from the team.

quirks: Insists on wearing the same lucky pair of worn-out racing gloves, regardless of weather conditions.
Always eats a specific brand of British chocolate bar 30 minutes before every race.
Refuses to walk under ladders and will go to extreme lengths to avoid doing so.
famousQuote: "Sometimes, you gotta risk it for the biscuit. Even if the biscuit ends up in the gravel."
careerHighlight: Winning the British GT Championship in 2017, showcasing his raw talent and proving his ability to perform under pressure when everything aligned.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the Spa 24 Hours in 2018, costing his team a certain victory and severely damaging his reputation.
